BiblicalUsage: A prisoner, one who is bound — asiyr appears in Joseph's prison, where the keeper committed all the prisoners into his hand, and in the Psalm, where God bringeth out those which are bound with chains. Zechariah turns the word into a promise: 'Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope.'
TheologicalSignificance: God hears the groaning of the prisoner and sets him free — I hold that as a picture of the gospel itself. And Zechariah's phrase is one I love: prisoners, yes, but prisoners of hope.
RelatedPeople: Joseph, Son of Jacob; King David; Zechariah the Prophet
